behaviors.name: Profanity Directed at Agent
behaviors.short_description: The caller aims profane or abusive language at the agent personally, rather than at the situation.
behaviors.detailed_description: To qualify, the speech must contain profanity or crude insults whose target is the agent as a person — name-calling, degrading labels, or profane commands addressed to the agent (e.g. insults attached to 'you'). General swearing about the company, product, or situation does not qualify on its own. The assessment must rely only on the language present in the clips, without inferred context.

behaviors.name: Sarcasm or Mockery
behaviors.short_description: The speaker uses sarcasm, rhetorical ridicule, or mocking comparisons to belittle the other party.
behaviors.detailed_description: To qualify, the speech must include statements whose intended meaning is the opposite of, or dismissive of, their literal content — rhetorical questions used as ridicule, absurd comparisons meant to demean (e.g. comparing the company's operations to a circus), or exaggerated imitation of the other party. Straightforward complaints or angry demands without ridicule do not qualify.
